newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Cement unit to launch naphtha project.
newsitem.headline: Siam Cement unit to launch naphtha project.

text.p: Siam Cement Plc's Siam Cement Chemicals Co unit said on Wednesday it planned to enter a joint venture with three Thai companies and a Japanese firm in a 5.22 billion baht ($200.77 million) naphtha plant project.

Siam Cement Chemical said it would team up with Rattanarat Group, the Siam Commercial Bank Plc, Tuntex (Thailand) Plc 's Tuntex Petrochemical Co Ltd unit, and Japan's Itochu Corp in the project due to start production in 1999.

Siam Cement Chemicals will hold a 40 percent stake in the Petrochain Co joint venture with Rattanarat Group owning 25 percent, Itochu 15 percent, and Siam Commercial and Tuntex Petrochemical 10 percent each.

The company said the plant, to be built in southeastern Rayong province, will have an annual production capacity of 700,000 tonnes of light naphtha, 990,000 tonnes of heavy naphtha, 220,000 tonnes of jet oil, 360,000 tonnes of high speed diesel and 200,000 tonnes of other products.
